Data coverage

—

How to read this dashboard

2026 Season. The four full-time Joe Gibbs Racing drivers in 2026 (2026 summary and Driver stats), race-level detail (Races, Speed, Points, Pit road, Competitors), a 2027 track preview and their O'Reilly/Xfinity seasons from 2024 to 2026, on any team (Year over year).

JGR Drivers. One page per full-time JGR driver (Sawalich, Crews, Jones, Gray) that pulls his 2026 numbers together: headline stats with field ranks, race by race, his radar, where his points went, track types, best and worst races, and his 2024–2026 seasons.

ROTY. Brent Crews' 2026 season against every Rookie of the Year and runner-up rookie since 2012: season stats (Rookie of the Year tab), start-by-start results and loop data (Race by race), the rookie against his own teammates (Teammates) and how long drivers took to win (First win).

Series History. Every O'Reilly/Xfinity points race 2011–2026: wins, poles, stage wins and laps led by team, team results by season and pole and starting-spot conversion (Teams); JGR season by season, where its wins came from and JGR against JRM (JGR history); and how many cars were competitive each season (Competition).

Colors and ranks. JGR cars: #18 purple, #19 orange, #20 red, #54 green. On the ROTY tabs orange = Brent Crews and blue = Rookies of the Year or the series value. Ranks count 1 as best and ties share the better rank; "median" always means earlier seasons only, so the current season never moves its own benchmark.

Controls. Buttons above a chart switch its metric. Rookie of the Year figures count every race, superspeedways included. Click any table header to sort (again to reverse). Copy image puts a PNG of that card on the clipboard; where the browser blocks the clipboard the image opens with a download button.

2026 Season

Drivers. The four full-time JGR drivers (20 or more JGR starts): Sawalich #18, Crews #19, Jones #20, Gray #54. Part-time drivers of JGR cars (Bell, Briscoe, Ruggiero) count only in the team totals. Pole = started first. Results, poles and laps led come from the full-field race results.

Loop data and points (2026). ARP = average running position: where the driver ran, averaged over every lap of the race. Race-by-race ARP, % of laps run inside the top 5 and race points come from the 2026 NOS JGR Points Standings dashboard (NASCAR results, driver points and loop data); race points match ESPN. Season figures are averages of the race values. Stage points = race points minus finish points (win 55, 2nd 35, then one less per place, minimum 1), the same rule used on the Race by race tab; the standings dashboard's own stage-point column did not add up to its race points, so it is not used.

Driver / Team (car) switch. The driver table can show each JGR car across all 33 races instead of each driver. The #19 then includes Ruggiero (races 1–2), Briscoe (race 5) and Bell (race 6). For those four races ARP comes from the NASCAR Race Lap Summary, and race points are finish points plus stage points from its stage 1 and 2 positions (that rebuild matches official race points within a point in most races). % of laps inside the top 5 is not available for them, so the #19's figure covers Crews' 29 races.

Points with no DNF. Race points per race counting only races where the driver (or car) was running at the finish. A blank finishing status (four 2026 entries in races 31 and 33, all full distance) counts as running.

Rates. T5 % and T10 % = top-5 and top-10 finishes as a share of starts.

Charts. Race by race plots the raw value for every race; pick a driver to bring his line forward (the others turn gray), and lines break at races he missed. By track type groups 2026 races into superspeedway, intermediate, short/flat and road course and can show average start, finish, ARP, % laps inside the top 5, top-5 rate, laps led and race points per race. Every chart starts its value axis at 0. Driver rating is not used anywhere on this dashboard.

Team comparison. 2026 totals across every car each team entered. Wins, top 5s and laps led are ranked among all teams; average finish and top-5 rate among teams with 50 or more starts, so one-off entries don't skew the ranks. % laps T5 = the team's share of all laps run in the top 5, adding up each car's % of laps inside the top 5 in every race and dividing by five times the number of races.

Year over year. One card per driver shows his last three seasons with 5+ starts and the change from the season before (green = better). The chart, radar and table show each full-time 2026 JGR driver's 2024–2026 O'Reilly/Xfinity seasons, on any team (Jones's 2023 season still sets his 2024 change); the team shown is the one with most of his starts that year. Race points per race from 2016 (DriverAverages.com archive; empty when not points-eligible), stage points from 2017 (race points minus finish points, win 40 through 2025). ARP for 2024 and 2025 is the average of each race's Race Average Position from the NASCAR Race Lap Summaries in the Pace Conditions tracker, the same per-race figure the 2026 values use (they match the standings dashboard in all 128 JGR 2026 races); % of laps inside the top 5 is available for 2026 only: the Race Lap Summaries carry each car's average, high and low position but no per-lap positions, and rebuilding the order from their lap times did not match NASCAR's own average positions, so 2024–25 are left blank rather than estimated. The 2026 radar uses the Competitors radar's eight measures for the four JGR cars. JGR teammates scales each spoke from the worst of the four JGR cars (a third of the way out, so a last place with a small gap doesn't collapse to the center) to the best; Competitors scales it against the 14-car group, as on the Competitors tab. The dashed outline is the median of whichever group is selected. Seasons with fewer than 5 starts are left out of the chart and summary; hollow dots mark seasons with fewer than 15. Change = previous 5+-start season's average finish minus this one (positive = improved).

2026 summary. One card per full-time driver, written from the 2024–2026 race file. Ranks for average finish, ARP, pace rank and season points are among drivers with 20 or more 2026 starts; points are race plus stage points summed over the season (no playoff reset), ranked only where driver points cover at least 80% of a driver's starts. DNF cost = finish points at his ARP (rounded) minus the finish points he scored, in races not running at the end. Track types need two or more starts to count. The 2025 comparison needs five or more 2025 starts. Regular season = races 1–24, playoffs = races 25–33. Owner points per race and their rank count every race the car ran, whoever drove. Conversion counts races with a top-5 green-flag pace rank and races with an ARP of 10 or better. Top JGR finisher = best finish among the four full-time JGR drivers in that race.

2024–2026 race file. One row per car per race for 2024–2026, built from NASCAR's Race Lap Summary reports in the Pace Conditions folder (car number, finish, laps, Race Average Position, green-flag pace ranks, % of laps under the P5 average) joined to the results and points data. The lap summary's Race Average Position matches the standings ARP in all 128 JGR 2026 races. The Races, Speed, Points, Competitors and 2027 preview tabs all read this file.

Races tab. Every 2026 race with all four JGR cars side by side. The #19 '25 and '24 columns match each 2026 race to the same track and the same visit (first or second trip there that season), whoever drove the #19. Italic = a part-time driver in the car. #19 vs others = the #19's value against the average of the #18, #20 and #54 that race, in the #19's favor. The teammate chart plots the same gap race by race; bars are green where the #19 did better, red where it did worse.

Speed. Green-flag pace rank = the car's rank in the lap summary's Filtered Race Avg LT (green-flag laps only), which tracks ARP closely (correlation 0.86). Short-run rank = each car's average of laps 2–6 of every green run, ranked in the field (correlation with ARP 0.65). Fast-lap rank = rank of the car's single fastest lap. % laps < P5 = share of the car's laps quicker than the fifth-place car's average lap. Pace vs finish = average finish minus average pace rank; positive means the car finished worse than it ran. Long-run pace was tested and dropped: it barely tracked results (correlation 0.1 or lower) because traffic and cautions swamp it.

Where the points went. For each race, the finish points a driver would have scored finishing at his ARP (rounded) are compared with the finish points he did score (55 for a 2026 win, otherwise 37 minus finish, minimum 1). Races not running at the end count as lost to DNFs; in races running at the end, finishing behind ARP counts as lost at the finish and ahead of it as gained. Stage points are shown but not part of the gap. Only the full-time driver's races count, so Crews has 29.

Qualifying vs race and consistency. Start → ARP = average start minus ARP (positive = ran ahead of where he started); ARP → finish = ARP minus average finish (positive = finished ahead of where he ran). Finish spread = standard deviation of finishes. Within 5 of ARP = races finished within five spots of the running position. Stage points per stage uses two scoring stages a race.

Pit road. From the season pages of NASCAR's Pit Road Report for the last race of 2024, 2025 and 2026: average stop time and its rank, net positions gained or lost on pit road over the season, and median green-flag entry time loss. Pit road figures follow the car number, not the driver. The chart shows only cars the report ranks, top 20 plus any JGR car below that.

Competitors. 2026 by car number for the four JGR cars and the leading cars in the owner standings, so shared rides count once. Points and stage points per race are owner-style: finish points plus stage points from each car's Stage 1 and Stage 2 positions in the Race Lap Summary, whoever drove, so cars shared with Cup drivers (#1, #88) count all 33 races. Checked against official driver points where both exist: 720 of 788 races match exactly and 762 within a point.

2027 tracks. The 2027 schedule from the 2026–2027 schedule PDF. Each round shows every JGR driver's 2024–2026 O'Reilly results at that track, in any car (a different car number is marked). A second visit to a track uses the same history as the first. North Wilkesboro has no series history in the data. The best-finish chart lists 2026 drivers with two or more starts there: the top 12 plus any JGR driver.

Remembered choices. The page remembers the last tab and every button choice in this browser, so it opens where you left it. Clearing site data resets it.

ROTY

Rookie of the Year margins. Winner and runner-up rookie from season pages, NASCAR and Jayski announcements and published rookie standings. All points and margins are cumulative season points, so the playoff reset (2016–2025) never counts. Cumulative points for 2016–2025 are summed race by race (finish plus stage points, no playoff points) from ESPN and racing-reference. For 2011–2015 and 2026 no reset applied to either rookie, so final points are cumulative. ESPN shows 10-point penalties for Byron (2017) and Bell (2018); they are not deducted. Both 2021 rookies ran part-time.

2011 class excluded from stat comparisons. Timmy Hill (Rookie of the Year) and Blake Koch (runner-up) ran back-of-field seasons with no top-10 finishes that skew every median and chart, so they are left out of the rookie stat, race-by-race, teammate and loop-data comparisons. Their points margin stays in the margin chart and table.

Rookie stat lines. From racing-reference career pages, checked against ESPN, Wikipedia and season reviews. Comparisons use rates per start; the scatter chart shows seasons with 10 or more starts. Crews' 2026 average start and finish are calculated from his race results.

Race logs. Every start for each Rookie of the Year, runner-up rookie and the 2026 class. Positions gained = start minus finish. DNF = not running at the finish; DNF rate and finish when running are shown only when the finishing status is known for most starts. Stage points (2017 on) = race points minus finish points. Track types: superspeedway (Daytona, Talladega, and Atlanta from its reconfiguration), road course, short/flat (up to a mile and a quarter) and intermediate.

Average running position and loop data. Average running position (weighted by laps), driver rating and share of laps in the top 15, from racing-reference loop-data pages and frcs.pro loop box scores. Running position shows where a driver ran all race rather than where he finished. Every Rookie of the Year and runner-up season has loop data. The 2011–2017 seasons come from racing-reference driver loop pages, where each race's average position is a whole number; four races whose listed average falls outside that race's high and low position (two for Austin Dillon 2012, two for Daniel Hemric 2017) are capped at the nearer limit. Crews' 2026 figure covers all of his starts.

Teammates. Each rookie season is compared with every other driver the same team entered that season, weighted by starts. Gap is in the rookie's favor: positions for average finish, percentage points for top-5 and top-10 rates. Average running position comes from each teammate's season loop data and is shown only when every teammate has it, which covers the Rookies of the Year from 2019 on. The tab shows Rookies of the Year only.

First win. Cup drivers: the 2026 full-time Cup roster with the O'Reilly/Xfinity start number of each driver's first series win, each count checked against the full race-by-race archive (two corrected: Erik Jones won in start 9, Chase Briscoe in start 14). O'Reilly drivers: everyone with 20 or more starts in 2026, with career series starts counted from 1982 on; drivers without a win are shown at their career starts so far. Brent Crews sits among the winners at his starts so far, as on the Cup chart. Both charts share one height and an axis that stops at 100 starts; longer waits run to the edge and are labeled with the real count.

Known gaps. Briscoe's 2019 laps led differ between racing-reference and ESPN (racing-reference used). Erik Jones's 2016 average start is not confirmed. Hemric's 2017 laps led and average start are incomplete. Sources disagree on Chandler Smith's 2023 top 5s and Sammy Smith's 2023 poles (racing-reference used). Teammate running position is incomplete before 2019 (for example Allgaier 2017–18, Harvick 2012 and 2014), so those seasons are left out of that view.

Series History

Team attribution. Each result counts for the team that entered the car in that race. Stewart-Haas Racing and Haas Factory Team, Penske Racing and Team Penske, and Turner Motorsports and Turner Scott Motorsports are each one organization. The share chart names the nine teams with the most success and groups the rest.

Poles. The car that started first in each race, from the full-field starting positions, so a race set by metrics or a qualifying rainout still counts its first-place starter. Every race 2011–2026 has one pole.

Stage wins. Leader at the end of Stage 1 and Stage 2, from 2017 when stages began. The final stage is the race win and is not counted.

Competition. A car is a team plus car number, whoever drove it, so a car shared by several drivers counts once. Contender: top 5 in at least 20% of that season's races. Top-10 regular: top 10 in at least half the races. Lead-lap finishers: cars completing the winner's lap count. Top team = most wins that season.

Checks. Every season has one winner per race and, from 2017, two stage winners per race. Laps led in each race equal the race length, except a few races one lap off in the source and the 2026 gaps listed under Data coverage.

Sources

Race source. 2011–2021: the DriverAverages.com race archive, distributed by the nascaR.data project (full fields with team, laps, laps led, stage finishes and driver rating); it matches the independently built 2022–25 results on every win and lap led. 2022–2026: race-by-race results from racing-reference.info, Wikipedia race articles, Jayski, ESPN and AP; 2026 full fields from Wikipedia and ESPN with driver ratings from frcs.pro and racing-reference loop data.

Rookie data. Rookie stat lines and race logs from racing-reference, ESPN, Wikipedia, frcs.pro and race reports. Season loop data for rookies and their teammates from racing-reference loop-data pages and frcs.pro box scores; per-race superspeedway loop data from racing-reference race loop pages and frcs.pro.

Career counts. First-win start numbers and career starts and wins for Cup and O'Reilly drivers are counted from the full race-by-race archive (1982 on) plus 2026 results. Driver ratings on the Teammates tab come from per-race ratings in the same archive.
